findings.title: New 'honest' tip 'Every comparison you run is saved in History.' (EN + AR) is false for Link-mode comparisons
findings.evidence: src/i18n/en.json loading.tip.save_offline and results.tips.save_offline = "Every comparison you run is saved in History."; AR twin = "every comparison you run is saved in the history". loading.tip.save_offline is one of the three DEFAULT_COMPARISON_TIP_KEYS (LoadingScreenVariants.tsx:176-180). HomeScreen draws a single loader overlay for every mode (HomeScreen.tsx:1150-1160, LoadingScreenVariants mode="comparison", default tips). runUrlCompare calls setLoading(true) at :551. Link mode is a first-class Home tab (testID home-mode-link, :1063-1073) and pasting a URL switches to it automatically (:921). The backend never saves a Link compare: url_routes.py:199-205 hands the compare_from_urls result to save_comparison_and_track_cohort, and save_comparison returns early unless _validate_renderable(payload) holds (database_service.py:431). That gate needs payload.metadata.query (:320-321), and compare_from_urls' success return has no metadata key (url_extraction_service.py:680-688). This is issue #340, still open at b965c63b. Probe (AST-extracted _validate_renderable, no app import), output in scratchpad adv-b3a-truth/probe_link_persist_out.txt: `compare_from_urls success-return keys: ['success', 'products', 'comparison', 'winner_index', 'recommendation', 'key_differences', 'category_used', 'source_urls']` / `has metadata key: False` / `_validate_renderable(link payload) = False` / `_validate_renderable(same + metadata.query) = True`. Result: a user running a Link compare is told it is saved, is billed for it (record_lifetime_comparison at url_routes.py:207-210), and never finds it in History. That is the same class as the 'even offline' promise this unit was written to remove. The copy came from spec 4.1, and the RED fixture b3a_copy.json pins it through r26, so GREEN followed the contract and the fix needs an orchestrator ruling.
findings.fix: Fixture + catalog amendment, ruled the way GA2 was: e.g. EN "Comparisons you type or snap are saved in History." with an AR twin that has no diacritics (A8). Alternative: keep a mode-neutral claim only once #340 (compare_from_urls emitting metadata.query) has shipped. Re-run honestCopy r26/r28 and copy-policy after the amendment.

findings.title: Results CohortBadge still shows a peer-proof claim the survey cannot back (pre-existing, outside the diff, same class as A13)
findings.evidence: en.json:759 results.cohort_badge = "{{count}}+ shoppers in {{governorate}} leaned the same way." The AR twin says they 'leaned to the same option'. It renders on Results (CohortBadge.tsx:64) whenever cohort_summary is present (ENABLE_COHORT_PERSONALIZATION is ON in prod, ruling A15). peer_count is demographics_profile.cohort_match.n (structured_comparison_service.py ~5472-5497): the number of survey respondents in the cohort (data/cohort_priors.json: total_responses 388, cohort keys age|gender|governorate|language). It is not a count of people who picked the winner, although CohortBadge's own prop doc says 'Number of cohort peers who also picked the winner.' A13 allowed survey-backed counts only in survey framing ('Informed by a survey of GCC shoppers'). This string is not in A13's named list and the unit did not touch it, but the commit message presents the learning and peer claims as handled.
findings.fix: Owner/orchestrator ruling. Either reword in survey framing (e.g. "{{count}} survey respondents in {{governorate}} share your profile", EN + AR without diacritics) or hide the badge. Record it as a follow-up if it is out of B3-A scope.

findings.title: Privacy inventory adds 'Other' to five rows with no evidence or definition, and contradicts its own AI-training paragraph for rows 5 and 8
findings.evidence: docs/privacy-data-inventory.md rows 3, 4, 5, 8 and 12 gain 'Other' in Purposes, and the json fence mirrors it (w37 c3/c5 green). Every other purpose in these rows has an evidence anchor (e.g. 'Personalization (anchors at 89f2dc6a)', 'Analytics (anchors at dfbda511)'). 'Other' has none. The doc's header says the App Store labels are filled FROM this file. Here the file was filled from the published labels (spec 2.5), so the rationale is missing. The doc's only candidate meaning, the 'Used to train AI models: YES' paragraph, names rows 3, 4 and 12 only. Nothing in the doc says why SearchHistory (row 5) or ProductInteraction (row 8, events to /api/v1/events, never sent to OpenAI) carry 'Other'. The manifest now matches the published label, which is the unit's goal; the gap is the engineering source of truth.
findings.fix: Add one sentence per row, or one paragraph, stating what 'Other' covers (e.g. the OpenAI data-sharing programme for 3/4/5/12). For row 8, either state the flow or record 'mirrors the published label pending owner confirmation'. Docs-only change, no test impact.

findings.title: 'GCC shoppers' survey framing (allowed by A13) rests on 388 responses keyed only by Bahrain governorates
findings.evidence: data/cohort_priors.json: version 1.0, total_responses 388. Every cohort key is age|gender|{Capital,Muharraq,Northern,Southern}|language, and the 'all' aggregate's demographics dict is empty (no country dimension). The new copy says 'Informed by a survey of GCC shoppers' (s13/s15 subtitles, loading.cohort.caption) and 'Based on answers from real GCC shoppers' (s12.bullet_1). s12.bullet_2 'Calibrated for the GCC - not the global average.' is kept, though it falls inside A13's named range :631-633. True in the narrow sense (Bahrain is in the GCC) and explicitly ruled acceptable by A13, but it implies GCC-wide breadth. Also: on Step 14 the counter chip now shows a bare cohort n with no label above the caption 'Informed by a survey of GCC shoppers', which reads as the survey size (e.g. 37 vs 388 total).
findings.fix: Owner's call. Optionally 'a survey of Bahrain shoppers', or keep it as ruled.

findings.title: Two new marketing absolutes are looser than the pipeline guarantees
findings.evidence: loading.tip.cross_checks / results.tips.retailers = "MYEZ checks retailers across the GCC for each product." and onboarding.s3.subtitle = "Side-by-side comparisons with prices from GCC retailers." A price can be a Tier-3 training-data estimate (estimated: true), a converted_usd price from a non-GCC host, or a 24 h cache hit with no live retailer check. Results itself can say 'Checked across 1 retail source.' s12.bullet_3 'Your own priorities shape every verdict' has the same 'every' shape. These read as house voice, not as false promises; noted for the owner's native read.
findings.fix: None required. Optionally soften: 'MYEZ checks GCC retailers for prices' / 'prices from GCC retailers where available'.

findings.title: GA2 Latin 'OpenAI' in the AR purpose strings was not applied; GREEN's stated reason is verified
findings.evidence: __tests__/config/nativeBundle.w37.test.ts:1410 u11 asserts `latin: /[A-Za-z]/.test(value)` is false for locales/ar.json purpose strings (:1438), and nativeStrings.b3a.test.ts:29 OPENAI_AR is the Arabic transliteration. findings.fix: Orchestrator rules: either amend u11 + OPENAI_AR together (GA1-style pin change) or withdraw GA2's Latin-brand half.
